ref_extractions.title: The ARSQ 2.0 reveals age and personality effects on mind-wandering experiences
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper is about the Amsterdam Resting-State Questionnaire (ARSQ) for measuring mind-wandering and its relationship to personality traits. It involves online questionnaire data from the Netherlands Sleep Registry, not EEG recordings. The dataset ds004587 contains visual illusion EEG data with 64-channel recordings at 10kHz, which is entirely different from this resting-state questionnaire study.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Study uses online questionnaires (ARSQ) from NSR database, no EEG data involved.

ref_extractions.title: Interpreting Black-Box Models: A Review on Explainable Artificial Intelligence
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a comprehensive review article on Explainable AI (XAI) methods for interpreting machine learning models. It has no connection to EEG neuroscience, visual perception, or the openneuro_ds004587 dataset. The paper focuses entirely on computational/AI interpretability topics with no biological signal processing content.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Pure XAI review paper; no EEG, neuroimaging, or experimental data analysis.

ref_extractions.title: Automatic acoustic detection of birds through deep learning: The first Bird Audio Detection challenge
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes a data challenge for automatic bird acoustic detection using deep learning on audio recordings. It is about passive acoustic monitoring of birds, completely unrelated to human EEG recordings or visual illusion paradigms. The dataset ds004587 contains human EEG data from visual illusion experiments, which has no overlap with this bioacoustic detection study.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Bird audio detection challenge; no EEG or human experimental data.

ref_extractions.title: Serial dependence in visual perception: A review
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article about serial dependence in visual perception, discussing how recent visual history influences current perception. While it relates to visual perception broadly, it does not use or reference the openneuro_ds004587 dataset specifically. The paper reviews existing literature on psychophysical effects but contains no original EEG data from this dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper on serial dependence; no use of ds004587 dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Functional Imaging of Numerical Processing in Adults and 4-y-Old Children
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This fMRI study investigates numerical processing in adults and 4-year-old children using functional magnetic resonance imaging. It focuses on the intraparietal sulcus involvement in numerical cognition. The dataset ds004587 contains EEG recordings from visual illusion experiments, which is entirely different from this numerical fMRI study.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: fMRI study of numerical cognition; no EEG data or visual illusion paradigms.

ref_extractions.title: Virtual Reality for Enhanced Ecological Validity and Experimental Control in the Clinical, Affective and Social Neurosciences
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is a review article discussing the potential of virtual reality environments for enhancing ecological validity in clinical, affective, and social neuroscience research. While it touches on neuroscience topics, it does not use or reference the openneuro_ds004587 dataset. The paper is conceptual and discusses VR methodologies without presenting original EEG data from the visual illusion dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Review paper on VR in neuroscience; no experimental use of ds004587 dataset.

feasibility_reason: Although this is a legitimate OpenNeuro dataset with a described paradigm (visual illusion perceptual judgments), it fails feasibility criteria because (1) no reference is rated 'relevant' or 'partial' to support the task, and (2) critically, the events.tsv contains no stimulus/response trial events—only administrative/artifact markers—making it impossible to construct stimulus-locked epochs from the EEG data alone without uncertain behavioral log recovery.
